title: 6 BORING Garage Businesses Anyone Can Start (Most Get Busier When It Gets Cold)
promo_conflict: Harry's own furniture and knife results are presented alongside mostly sourced examples; no paid promotion is disclosed.

idea.name: Furniture flipping
idea.one_liner: Buy low-cost solid-wood furniture, refinish it in a garage, and resell it to local buyers.
idea.customer: Local second-hand furniture buyers, including people moving or setting up a home.
idea.offer: Refinished furniture, listed for local pickup.
idea.revenue_model: Buy furniture cheaply, add materials and labor, then resell at a markup.

stated_problem.quote: Families outgrow them every couple of years, and a clean, safe, tuned kids bike sells fast every spring.

idea.name: Bicycle refurb flipping
idea.one_liner: Buy unwanted bikes cheaply in winter, refurbish them, and resell them when spring demand returns.
idea.customer: Local bike buyers, including families buying children's bikes.
idea.revenue_model: Buy used bikes, spend on parts and repairs, then resell at a markup.

key_quotes.quote: A Seattle hobbyist named Jeff puts $60 into an old touring bike and sold it for $200.
The Smart Rhythm is buying cheap in winter when nobody wants a bike and selling in spring when everybody does.
